blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A generator's output for value and safety, both maximized, includes the plans (value 900, safety 50) and (value 900, safety 62). What should the pairwise check report?

options.text: Nothing, since (900, 50) and (900, 62) tie on value, so neither dominates
options.says: Dominating needs at least as good on both and better on one; a tie on value with more safety is enough.

options.text: Nothing, since the generator has already removed dominated plans
options.says: A plain floor can return a weakly efficient plan; that is why the list is checked before it is read.

options.text: A solver failure, since (900, 50) and (900, 62) should not tie on value
options.says: Ties on one objective are ordinary; the NPV-0 vegetation variant had many.

options.text: A dominated plan, since (900, 62) ties on value and has more safety
options.says: Right: (900, 50) is dominated and does not belong on the frontier.

origin.section: Generate the Frontier Once, and Check That No Point Dominates Another

questions.stem: Three supported plans, in order of risk removed: A (NPV 1,000, risk 100), B (NPV 960, risk 180), C (NPV 800, risk 220). What are the prices of the steps A to B and B to C, in NPV given up per unit of risk?

options.text: 0.5 for A to B, then 4.0 for B to C, so the second step is dearer
options.says: Right: 40 / 80 = 0.5 and 160 / 40 = 4.0; along the hull the price rises.

options.text: 2.0 for A to B, then 0.25 for B to C, so the second step is cheaper
options.says: That divides risk by NPV; the price is NPV given up per unit of risk gained.

options.text: 40 for A to B, then 160 for B to C, the NPV each step gives up
options.says: That is the cost of the step, not its price; divide by the risk gained.

options.text: 0.5 for A to B, then 1.7 for A to C, both measured from plan A
options.says: Each step's price compares neighbours; measuring from A mixes two steps into one.

origin.section: State Each Step as a Price: NPV Given Up per Dollar of Risk Removed

questions.stem: Along the supported plans the step prices are 0.20, 0.30, 0.35, 2.10 and 2.40 of NPV per unit of risk. With the lesson's factor of two, where is the knee?

options.text: After the first step, since 0.30 is already more than 0.20
options.says: A knee needs the price to at least double; 0.30 is one and a half times 0.20.

options.text: At the plan between the 0.35 step and the 2.10 step
options.says: Right: 2.10 is six times 0.35, and no other neighbouring pair doubles.

options.text: At the plan with the most risk, since its step costs the most
options.says: A knee is where the price jumps, not where it is highest; 2.40 is close to 2.10.

options.text: Nowhere, since prices always rise along the supported plans
options.says: They do rise, which is why a knee is defined by how sharply, not whether.

origin.section: A Knee Is Where the Price Jumps

concepts: a supported plan where the next step's price at least doubles
